key_insight: A curated benchmark of real failed agent executions plus a grounded-theory failure taxonomy enables precise localization of the single critical step that caused an AI agent run to fail.
problem_solved: Localizing failures in probabilistic, long-horizon, multi-agent agent executions is hard because errors propagate across noisy tools and interactions; the paper provides labeled data and a taxonomy to diagnose where and why runs fail.
method: Manually annotate 115 failed agent trajectories spanning API workflows, incident management, and open-ended web/file tasks.
Derive a cross-domain failure taxonomy using grounded theory, and label each trajectory with the critical failure step and a category.
Release the benchmark to enable systematic diagnosis, evaluation, and future tooling for failure localization in agent systems.
impact: Provides practitioners with a structured dataset and taxonomy to benchmark and develop diagnostics, debuggers, and robustness techniques for complex AI agents, accelerating reproducible failure analysis and tool improvement.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram of an agent execution highlighting the annotated critical failure step in red

paper_title: AgentRx: Diagnosing AI Agent Failures from Execution Trajectories
paper_authors: Shraddha Barke, Arnav Goyal, Alind Khare, Avaljot Singh, Suman Nath
